topic: How does interleaved array element spacing affect coverage patterns and grating lobe suppression in Ka-band satellite links?
consensus_response: Interleaved array element spacing affects coverage patterns and grating lobe suppression by influencing the array factor. Tighter spacing reduces grating lobes but increases complexity, while polarization diversity and adaptive beamforming enhance interference mitigation. Balancing these factors optimizes performance.
reference_context: Ka-band satellites use spot beams for high-throughput services, requiring precise beamforming and grating lobe suppression.
